items.title: See if you qualify for the $53 million EmblemHealth and City of New York senior care copay class action settlement - Claim Depot
items.reason: This item reports a $53 million class action settlement involving EmblemHealth (a major payer) and the City of New York over senior care copay practices, which constitutes payer litigation and enforcement directly relevant to the topic rubric.
items.summary: EmblemHealth and the City of New York have reached a $53 million class action settlement addressing senior care copay practices. The settlement provides compensation to class members who may have been overcharged or improperly billed copays for senior care services. This enforcement action affects EmblemHealth policyholders and senior beneficiaries in New York and represents a significant liability resolution for the payer related to claims-handling and billing practices, which revenue-cycle teams must track for compliance and claims-processing implications.

items.title: Top Boston hospitals clash over Medicare Advantage network after split - STAT
items.reason: A dispute between major hospitals and payers over Medicare Advantage network inclusion/exclusion directly affects revenue-cycle operations, network credentialing, and claims processing, fitting the topic's scope on payer policies that penalize providers over network status.
items.summary: Top Boston hospitals are clashing with Medicare Advantage insurers following a network reorganization, with hospitals disputing their inclusion or exclusion from payer networks. The dispute centers on Medicare Advantage network configuration decisions that affect hospital reimbursement and patient access. This type of provider-payer conflict over network status directly impacts revenue-cycle teams' credentialing processes, claim acceptance rates, and contract negotiations, as network placement determines whether claims are processed in-network or subject to higher cost-sharing or denial.
